title: Frontend mid domain event loop async
topic: Frontend mid domain event loop async
question: Explain how the JavaScript event loop handles asynchronous work, and specifically the difference between microtasks and macrotasks.
idealAnswer:
JavaScript runs on a single thread with a call stack, the event loop coordinates running code, handling events, and executing queued asynchronous callbacks without blocking that thread

Macrotasks (also called tasks) include things like setTimeout callbacks, DOM events, and I/O, each macrotask runs to completion before the loop moves on

Microtasks include promise callbacks (.then/.catch/.finally) and queueMicrotask, the microtask queue is fully drained after each macrotask finishes and before the next macrotask or render, even before the next setTimeout(fn, 0)

This is why Promise.resolve().then(...) logs before a setTimeout(fn, 0), even though both are 'async', microtasks always get priority over the next macrotask

Because the loop is single-threaded, a long-running synchronous task blocks everything, including rendering and other callbacks, which is why expensive synchronous work causes a frozen/unresponsive UI

async/await is syntactic sugar over promises, an async function still runs synchronously up to the first await, and code after await is scheduled as a microtask continuation
